description: Authored Core, research, ownership and sequencing inputs for the master capability registry. Shipped module identity remains runtime-derived in rgx-api.catalog.json; domain-research.json owns native-domain gap evidence.

coreSystems.name: Framework and module registration
coreSystems.purpose: One framework object, named module registration, aliases, getters and availability-aware lookup.
coreSystems.performance: Registry lookup is direct table access with alias fallback.
consumerCoverage: All registered modules and RGX consumers
coreSystems.acceptanceCriteria: Preserve one registry and the frozen public global surface.

coreSystems.name: Lifecycle and initialization
coreSystems.purpose: Readiness, post-load initialization, TryInit, database adoption and convenience wrappers.
coreSystems.performance: Initialization runs once per framework load; no recurring lifecycle driver.
coreSystems.acceptanceCriteria: Keep file loading, registration, initialization and client availability as distinct states.

coreSystems.name: Client compatibility and capability gates
coreSystems.purpose: Centralized client detection, normalized API adapters, module support and restricted-value boundaries.
coreSystems.performance: Capability probes are computed once at load where possible.
coreSystems.acceptanceCriteria: Verify each API by flavor/build/source and fail closed on unknown or restricted values.

coreSystems.name: Declarative addon factory
coreSystems.purpose: Compile RGXAddon declarations into scoped addon objects without a second runtime or DSL.
coreSystems.performance: Declarations are validated before resource registration; lazy UI rendering stays in UI.
coreSystems.acceptanceCriteria: Keep runtime, schema, documentation, generators and validators congruent.

coreSystems.name: Persistence and profiles
coreSystems.purpose: SavedVariables, defaults, migrations, profile-aware proxies, import/export and adoption.
coreSystems.performance: Proxy access and migrations follow existing budgeted lifecycle; no new polling.
coreSystems.acceptanceCriteria: Preserve false versus nil, nested defaults, profiles, migrations and SavedVariables lifecycle.

coreSystems.name: Events, messages and emitters
coreSystems.purpose: Native events, unit events, internal messages and module-local failure-isolated emitters.
coreSystems.performance: One dispatcher and deferred native registration; no consumer event frames.
coreSystems.acceptanceCriteria: Preserve failure isolation and deferred native registration; evaluate aggregation before adding it.

coreSystems.name: Scheduling and asynchronous runtime work
coreSystems.purpose: One-shot/repeating timers, budgeted scheduling, hooks, combat queue and safe operations.
coreSystems.performance: Hidden OnUpdate driver sleeps with no active timers; existing per-frame/time budgets apply.
coreSystems.acceptanceCriteria: Benchmark structural scheduler changes and preserve timer labels and failure isolation.

coreSystems.name: Slash commands
coreSystems.purpose: Centralized consumer slash registration and the framework /rgxf command surface.
coreSystems.performance: Registration is one-time with normalized aliases.
coreSystems.acceptanceCriteria: Keep slash registration centralized and avoid SLASH_ globals in consumers.

coreSystems.name: Shared utilities and chat output
coreSystems.purpose: String/table/math helpers, throttling, prefixes, consumer chat and login preferences.
coreSystems.performance: Small synchronous helpers; no background work implied.
coreSystems.acceptanceCriteria: Do not turn small utilities into competing public subsystems.

coreSystems.name: Framework defaults
coreSystems.purpose: Framework debug, version and default font configuration.
testCoverage: Static source reconciliation only; no runtime consumer is claimed by this record
coreSystems.acceptanceCriteria: Verify actual default consumers before recording adoption or extending configuration.

coreSystems.name: Contract and authoring compatibility
coreSystems.purpose: Contract format handshake, declarative schema/engine and authoring compatibility.
coreSystems.performance: Version checks run at load; shared engine remains development tooling.
coreSystems.acceptanceCriteria: One canonical contract with no MCP-only semantics or version-number duplication.

coreSystems.name: Diagnostics and error isolation
coreSystems.purpose: Structured warnings, callback error containment and stable diagnostic labels.
coreSystems.performance: Error paths are exceptional and isolated from unrelated consumers.
coreSystems.acceptanceCriteria: Hostile formatting and error-handler acquisition cannot break shared dispatch.

candidates.name: Master capability registry and conformance gate
candidates.purpose: Persistent capability ownership, gap status, evidence, replacement mapping and implementation sequencing.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Generated registry matches runtime catalog plus authored research and remains CI-congruent.

candidates.name: Event aggregation and dirty-state batching
candidates.purpose: Coalesce high-frequency events without losing payloads or changing consumer semantics.
candidates.publicContract: RGX:RegisterEvent / RegisterUnitEvent optional { bucket, key } options
candidates.performance: 10,000-event harness: one callback per burst, bounded pending keys and measured elapsed/heap deltas.
testCoverage: event-bucketing-check: latest/keyed/nil/failure/unregister/cap semantics plus 10,000-event baseline comparison
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Keep opt-in current-state semantics only; transition streams remain unbucketed and real-client timing is verified separately.

candidates.name: RGXTriggers library ownership correction
candidates.purpose: Align the generic clone-state store with library semantics while preserving its public contract.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Preserve module ID, global, getter, methods and state semantics across XML, catalog, tests and docs; audit consumers before moving.

candidates.name: Conditional trigger evaluation
candidates.purpose: Evaluate conditional rules over generic trigger state without duplicating domain events.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Resolve one owner and authoring model before implementing an evaluation engine.

candidates.name: Animation composition and glows
candidates.purpose: Transitions, fades, movement, pulses and button glows.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Use native animation/widget evidence and a current consumer before adding a public owner.

candidates.name: Addon communication
candidates.purpose: Queued, throttled addon messages with prioritization and channel discipline.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Establish a real consumer need and a safe channel/throttle contract first.

candidates.name: Differential synchronization
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Define data ownership, conflict rules and recovery semantics before transport work.

candidates.name: Structured serialization
candidates.purpose: General structured table encoding/decoding for import/export; any future extraction is a migration candidate, not a second owner.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Preserve general table round trips and evaluate any future extraction as a migration rather than a parallel serializer.

candidates.name: Transfer compression
candidates.purpose: Compact transferable data with chunking and reassembly.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Choose one data owner and evaluate native/simple algorithms, size and CPU cost before implementation.

candidates.name: Search and filtering
candidates.purpose: Query construction, indexing and filtering for items and other registries.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Define a reusable query contract and a concrete inventory or settings consumer.

candidates.name: Notifications and routing
candidates.purpose: Alerts, toasts and notification routing without per-consumer display plumbing.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Separate notification policy, routing and rendering before choosing a public contract.

candidates.name: Reusable unit-frame components
candidates.purpose: Composable unit-frame building blocks rather than a parallel oUF runtime.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Resolve Units ownership, frame security and a maintained consumer before component implementation.

candidates.name: Virtualized lists, tables and trees
candidates.purpose: Virtualized scrolling, sortable tables and tree views with bounded frame use.
candidates.performance: Benchmark frame reuse, allocation and scroll updates on large datasets.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Extend existing scroll/layout primitives and prove bounded allocations on long lists.

candidates.name: Transactional configuration
candidates.purpose: Apply, revert and reset workflows with searchable settings and confirmation paths.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Preserve profile semantics and visual restoration; do not build a second database.

candidates.name: Markdown and SimpleHTML content
candidates.purpose: Reusable markdown and SimpleHTML rendering for guides and dialogs.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Use native SimpleHTML where sufficient and define escaping/sanitization before a custom renderer.

candidates.name: Native Edit Mode integration
candidates.purpose: Screen snapping, alignment, docking and native Edit Mode integration.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Distinguish the shipped custom drag editor from native Edit Mode before extending the contract.

candidates.name: Keybinding registration and controls
candidates.purpose: Keybinding registration and user-facing keybinding controls.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Separate Core registration from UI controls and verify protected mutation rules.

candidates.name: Object and frame pooling
candidates.purpose: Reuse objects and frames to reduce allocation on high-churn interfaces.
candidates.performance: Requires allocation benchmarks and lifecycle/reset correctness before adoption.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Introduce pooling only for a measured hot path with complete reset semantics.

candidates.name: Optional data-pack architecture
candidates.purpose: Optional, load-on-demand datasets for spells, items, NPCs, quests, zones, travel, encounters, professions, collectibles, icons, sounds and atlases.
candidates.acceptanceCriteria: Require provenance, licensing, build compatibility and refresh process; do not enlarge the mandatory runtime without demonstrated need.

ownershipReviews.decision: Semantically a library; migrate only after consumer audit
ownershipReviews.rationale: Generic clone registry/diff/progress with no event subscriptions or flavor gate; preserve global/getter/API semantics.

ownershipReviews.currentOwner: modules/inventory/inventory.lua owns counts and consumer-supplied material arithmetic
ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: Inventory owns items/material counts; Equipment owns equipped state; Professions owns recipe domain state
ownershipReviews.decision: Do not merge item counts, equipment and recipes
ownershipReviews.rationale: Prevent a single items god-module and keep consumer recipe selection outside Inventory.

ownershipReviews.currentOwner: modules/combat/combat.lua owns combat state and narrow callbacks
ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: Combat for combat state; Encounters for encounter metadata/timeline; Instances for lockouts/difficulty
ownershipReviews.decision: Extend Combat only for intrinsic combat signals
ownershipReviews.rationale: EncounterJournal, live encounter state and instance lockouts are distinct domains.

ownershipReviews.currentOwner: No general Units owner; Auras/Combat/compat hold narrow unit operations
ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: Research a Units identity/state owner; keep Cast and specialized state separate
ownershipReviews.decision: Resolve unit identity, health/power secrecy and token comparability before APIs
ownershipReviews.rationale: Avoid duplicating Cast, Auras, Range, Group and Nameplate state.

ownershipReviews.currentOwner: modules/auras/auras.lua owns aura state and specific readiness
ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: Auras for aura state; Spells for spell metadata/cooldowns; Dispels for classification only if justified
ownershipReviews.decision: Do not turn Auras into a general Spells or ActionBars owner
ownershipReviews.rationale: Current CastReadiness is a narrow contract, not full cast or spell state.

ownershipReviews.currentOwner: Core has narrow party/raid helpers; no LFG owner
ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: Group for party/raid; Guild for guild/club; LFG as a separate queue domain if needed
ownershipReviews.decision: Separate roster, guild and queue state
ownershipReviews.rationale: Permissions, async state and lifecycle differ across these domains.

ownershipReviews.currentOwner: modules/worldmap/worldmap.lua owns coordinates, pins and nearest-place lookup
ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: WorldMap for map geometry/pins; Travel for taxi/navigation/summons only with consumer need
ownershipReviews.decision: Do not substitute geometric distance for spell range or taxi state
ownershipReviews.rationale: Map navigation, spell range and protected travel actions are different capabilities.

ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: Quest for quest state; Guides for guide/journal/tutorial content only if required
ownershipReviews.decision: Keep progression data separate from presentation guides
ownershipReviews.rationale: AdventureJournal and Tutorial references are incomplete and do not justify a guide runtime by themselves.

ownershipReviews.currentOwner: SharedMedia generic paths; Fonts/Textures/Sound specialized registries; Colors/Design color ownership
ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: SharedMedia for generic discovery/interoperability; specialized libraries for metadata/behavior
ownershipReviews.decision: Do not create an automatic unified mirror of specialized registries
ownershipReviews.rationale: SharedMedia scans sound only; Fonts, Textures and Sound own their specialized handles/defaults/application.

ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: Evaluate one serialization/data owner; charts belong in UI and keybinding controls in UI with Core registration
ownershipReviews.decision: Consolidate supporting capabilities instead of creating one directory per noun
ownershipReviews.rationale: The candidate count is not a mandate for new public namespaces.

replacementMatrix.rationale: One framework instance and registry; no LibStub version negotiation.
Declarative addon factory and lifecycle, not API-compatible emulation.
Central event/message/emitter dispatch.
Budgeted After/Every/CancelTimer driver.
Central secure post-hook owner.
Central slash registration.
Profiles, migrations and SavedVariables adoption.
Options and profile-aware controls, not an AceConfig compatibility layer.
Declarative options with existing UI composition.
Reusable widgets exist; complete AceGUI widget coverage is not claimed.
Framework-owned locale registry and overrides.
Failure-isolated messages and emitters.
Generic pack/path registration and interoperability; specialized behavior remains separate.
Observable data objects and notifications.
Minimap and compartment buttons.
Nested/native menu composition.
Countdown/progress components.
Map coordinates/pins exist; comprehensive HereBeDragons compatibility is not claimed.
General table serialization exists in Core; broader transport compatibility is not claimed.
Scoped opt-in latest-per-key bucketing with regression and burst evidence; not a universal AceBucket replacement.
Requires a real consumer and channel contract.
Throttling belongs to the communication owner.
Queue discipline belongs to the communication owner.
Differential sync and recovery are not implemented.
Core table serialization exists; a general LibSerialize-compatible surface is not claimed.
No compression owner is implemented.
Animation composition remains research.
Button glow belongs to the same animation research owner.
The shipped custom drag editor is not native Edit Mode integration.
Composed tooltips exist; LibQTip compatibility is not claimed.
Notification routing remains research.
Sink routing belongs to the same notification owner.
Theme/skin mechanisms exist; full Masque replacement is not claimed.
Display owns positioned elements; general frame discovery is not a separate public library.
Search contract and consumer are not established.
Query construction belongs to the same search owner.
Range semantics and secrecy require research; map distance is not a substitute.
Spell/action range needs one domain owner.
Spell metadata scope and native API differences are unresolved.
Talent/loadout models vary by client.
Group inspection and roster state need a bounded owner.
Do not create parallel group and communication contracts without a consumer.
Healing prediction and restricted values require native evidence.
Aura classification and protected dispel actions are separate concerns.
Secure action-button behavior is not implied by spell queries.
Travel data belongs in a provenance-controlled data pack.
Static quest data requires provenance and refresh rules.
Reusable components are a candidate, not an oUF-compatible runtime.

implementationSequence.rationale: Establish source-of-truth ownership and evidence before runtime expansion; delivered by this Phase 0 change.
Delivered scoped opt-in latest-per-key bucketing with ordering, payload, failure, cancellation and 10,000-event burst evidence.
Semantically justified but blocked on consumer audit and synchronized public-contract migration.
Interface expansion follows Core/resource ownership and requires a real long-list consumer and allocation benchmark.
Harden and scope the existing Core table serializer before any transport design; do not create a parallel owner.
Communication follows serialization and a maintained consumer rather than speculative transport APIs.
